fatal_errors: The proposed material and initial state are a single-phase MoNbTaTiV refractory HEA, whereas the target concerns as-cast, dual-phase FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The intervention is deformation temperature and strain rate rather than intermediate-temperature thermal aging.

The hypothesis invokes grain-boundary segregation and intergranular decohesion—the conventional-alloy mechanism the comparison was meant to distinguish—instead of L12 ordering, jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries, and plastic instability.
It does not predict the defining non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response, including minimum ductility near 600°C aging and recovery near 750°C.
The cited evidence establishes deformation-induced segregation in MoNbTaTiV but does not establish that this segregation reduces boundary cohesion or causes brittle fracture.
Temperature and strain rate are changed together, preventing attribution of any response to either variable independently.
explanation: The response offers an internally testable alternative hypothesis, with microscopy, fractography, mechanical measurements, and an explicit falsification rule. E1 supports the occurrence of deformation-induced segregation under relatively low deformation temperatures and high strain rates, while E2 supports a relationship between grain-boundary morphology and hot ductility in another HEA. However, neither citation validates the full claimed causal chain from deformation-induced segregation to reduced grain-boundary cohesion and embrittlement. Scientifically, the reconstruction misses every central feature of the target: AlCoCrFeNi2.1, its FCC+B2 eutectic microstructure, thermal aging in the 550–750°C window, enhanced L12 ordering, jagged phase-boundary tips, restricted cross-slip and planar slip, and the ductile-brittle-ductile transition. Its experiment could test its own alternative, but a factorial design varying temperature and strain rate independently and direct local cohesion or crack-initiation measurements would be needed for decisive causal discrimination.
